precepts.text: Under Josiah, money for the temple came from Manasseh, Ephraim and all the remnant of Israel.
precepts.point: The Lord sent a word into Jacob and it lighted on Israel, and all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Under Josiah, when the money for the house of God was brought to Hilkiah the high priest, it was “the money that was brought into the house of God, which the Levites that kept the doors had gathered of the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim, and of all the remnant of Israel, and of all Judah and Benjamin”.

Manasseh donated toward the temple in Jerusalem, and Ephraim donated too. Why “the remnant of Israel”? Because Assyria had taken most of them out of the land in waves; remnants remained, some idolatrous and some faithful. And that was during Josiah’s reign: whenever Judah is on point, Ephraim follows along.

Then Isaiah speaks to those same northern lands: “the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali”, afflicted “by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.” Zebulun came to keep the Passover in Hezekiah’s day, and Tobit was of Naphtali. Galilee of the Gentiles is where the northern kingdom resided, and they were called Gentiles. “The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light”: the people of verse 1, the northern kingdom.

“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”: unto us, not all. He is the Prince of Peace because he must bring peace between those who have hatred for each other, so that there is no more division between the two kingdoms. “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel. And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria”. The same Ephraim and Manasseh whose remnant gave to the house of God in Judah’s good days would see the light of the son born of Judah.

precepts.text: Better is a poor and wise child than an old and foolish king who will no more be admonished, the very lesson of these young kings.
precepts.point: In the eighth year of his reign, while yet young, he begins to seek after the God of David, and in the twelfth year he begins to purge Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, groves, and images.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

precepts.why:
“Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.” That is the very lesson of these young kings.

Compare the ages. Manasseh began at twelve, Amon at twenty two, and Josiah “was eight years old when he began to reign”, yet the youngest was the wisest. Josiah “did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the ways of David his father”.

“For in the eighth year of his reign, while he was yet young, he began to seek after the God of David his father: and in the twelfth year he began to purge Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, and the groves, and the carved images, and the molten images.” The wise child sought the Most High while the older kings before him would no more be admonished.

precepts.text: Josiah declining neither to the right nor left is the charge to Joshua: observe to do according to all the law, turn not from it, and meditate in it day and night that thy way may be prosperous.
precepts.point: In the eighth year of his reign, while yet young, he begins to seek after the God of David, and in the twelfth year he begins to purge Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, groves, and images.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

precepts.why:
The charge to Joshua: “Only be thou strong and very courageous, that thou mayest observe to do according to all the law, which Moses my servant commanded thee: turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that thou mayest prosper whithersoever thou goest.” And “thou shalt meditate therein day and night”, “for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.”

Josiah is that charge kept. He “walked in the ways of David his father, and declined neither to the right hand, nor to the left.” He observed to do according to the law, turned not from it, and so he reigned “in Jerusalem one and thirty years.”

precepts.text: Those who sanctify and purify themselves in the gardens behind one tree, eating swine's flesh and the abomination, shall be consumed together, the same garden and grove worship Josiah tears down.
precepts.point: He burns the bones of the priests upon their altars and cleanses Judah and Jerusalem, and does the same in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, then returns to Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

precepts.why:
“They that sanctify themselves, and purify themselves in the gardens behind one tree in the midst, eating swine’s flesh, and the abomination, and the mouse, shall be consumed together, saith the Lord.” That is the same garden and grove worship Josiah tore down.

“And they brake down the altars of Baalim in his presence; and the images, that were on high above them, he cut down; and the groves, and the carved images, and the molten images, he brake in pieces, and made dust of them, and strowed it upon the graves of them that had sacrificed unto them.” “And he burnt the bones of the priests upon their altars, and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.”

He did the same “in the cities of Manasseh, and Ephraim, and Simeon, even unto Naphtali”, and when he “had beaten the graven images into powder, and cut down all the idols throughout all the land of Israel, he returned to Jerusalem.” Those who worshipped in the groves were consumed together, as the Lord said.

precepts.text: This is the law which Moses set before the children of Israel, the same book of the law that was found in the house of the Lord.
precepts.point: Shaphan carries the book to the king and reads it before him, reporting that all committed to the servants is being done and the money delivered to the workmen.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

precepts.why:
“And this is the law which Moses set before the children of Israel”. That is the same book of the law that was found in the house of the Lord.

“And when they brought out the money that was brought into the house of the Lord, Hilkiah the priest found a book of the law of the Lord given by Moses.” The very Bible. He said, “I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord”, and delivered it to Shaphan the scribe.

Shaphan carried the book to the king and reported that “All that was committed to thy servants, they do it”, and the money was delivered “to the hand of the workmen.” Then he told the king, “Hilkiah the priest hath given me a book. And Shaphan read it before the king.” The law Moses set before Israel was set before the king again.

precepts.text: All Israel had transgressed the law, so the curse and oath written in the law of Moses was poured out upon them, for the Most High is righteous in all his works.
precepts.point: He knows great is the wrath of the Lord poured out because the fathers had not kept the word of the Lord to do all that is written in the book. To inquire of the Lord, one must go to a saint, a chosen prophet who has the word.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

precepts.why:
“Yea, all Israel have transgressed thy law, even by departing, that they might not obey thy voice; therefore the curse is poured upon us, and the oath that is written in the law of Moses the servant of God, because we have sinned against him.” The Lord “hath confirmed his words, which he spake against us”, “for the Lord our God is righteous in all his works which he doeth: for we obeyed not his voice.”

Josiah saw the same thing when he heard the book: “it came to pass, when the king had heard the words of the law, that he rent his clothes”, and said, “great is the wrath of the Lord that is poured out upon us, because our fathers have not kept the word of the Lord, to do after all that is written in this book.”

All Israel had transgressed the law, so the curse and oath written in the law of Moses was poured out upon them, and the Most High is righteous in it. Josiah knew it, so he sent to “enquire of the Lord for me, and for them that are left in Israel and in Judah”.

precepts.text: Call now, if there be any that will answer thee, and to which of the saints wilt thou turn; to learn the Bible you must go to one of the chosen.
precepts.point: He knows great is the wrath of the Lord poured out because the fathers had not kept the word of the Lord to do all that is written in the book. To inquire of the Lord, one must go to a saint, a chosen prophet who has the word.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

precepts.why:
“Call now, if there be any that will answer thee; and to which of the saints wilt thou turn?” To inquire of the Lord, one must go to a saint, a chosen prophet who has the word. To learn the Bible you must go to one of the chosen.

That is what Josiah did. He had the book read before him, but he did not stop there: he “commanded Hilkiah, and Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Abdon the son of Micah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah a servant of the king’s, saying, Go, enquire of the Lord for me”, “concerning the words of the book that is found”. He turned to one who could answer.

precepts.text: Humble yourself before the Most High and you find favour, and the mysteries are revealed to the meek and lowly, as they were to tender hearted Josiah.
precepts.point: But because Josiah's heart was tender and he humbled himself, wept, and rent his clothes, the Most High will gather him to his fathers in peace so his eyes will not see the evil to come.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

precepts.why:
“My son, go on with thy business in meekness; so shalt thou be beloved of him that is approved. The greater thou art, the more humble thyself, and thou shalt find favour before the Lord. Many are in high place, and of renown: but mysteries are revealed unto the meek. For the power of the Lord is great, and he is honoured of the lowly.”

Humble yourself before the Most High and you find favour, and the mysteries are revealed to the meek and lowly, as they were to tender-hearted Josiah. The king was great, and he humbled himself the more.

Huldah the prophetess declared evil upon Jerusalem, “even all the curses that are written in the book”, “Because they have forsaken me, and have burned incense unto other gods”. But to the king: “Because thine heart was tender, and thou didst humble thyself before God, when thou heardest his words against this place”, “and didst rend thy clothes, and weep before me; I have even heard thee also, saith the Lord.” That is the favour found by the humble.

precepts.text: The righteous perisheth and no man layeth it to heart, and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come, which is why Josiah is gathered in peace.
precepts.point: But because Josiah's heart was tender and he humbled himself, wept, and rent his clothes, the Most High will gather him to his fathers in peace so his eyes will not see the evil to come.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

precepts.why:
“The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart: and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.”

That is why Josiah is gathered in peace. The Lord said through Huldah, “Behold, I will gather thee to thy fathers, and thou shalt be gathered to thy grave in peace, neither shall thine eyes see all the evil that I will bring upon this place, and upon the inhabitants of the same.”

The wrath was coming upon Jerusalem and “shall not be quenched”, and the righteous king was taken away from the evil to come.
